{{c|{{sc|Ode 7. The {{tooltip|Hwang Î|Huáng Yí}}.}}}}
{{dhr|0%}}
{{smaller block/s}}
{{hanging indent/s}}
{{asc|Showing the rise of the [[Portal:Zhou dynasty|house of ''K''âu]] to the sovereignty of the kingdom through the favour of God, the achievements of kings [[w:King Tai of Zhou|Thâi]] and [[w:Ji, King of Zhou|''K''î]], and especially of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]].}}
{{hanging indent/e}}
{{smaller block/e}}

{{center block/s}}
Great is God,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Beholding this lower world in majesty.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He surveyed the four quarters (of the kingdom),{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Seeking for some one to give establishment to the people.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Those two earlier dynasties<ref>Those of [[Portal:Xia dynasty|Hsiâ]] and [[Portal:Shang dynasty|Shang]].</ref>{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Had failed to satisfy him with their government;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
So, throughout the various states,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He sought and considered{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
For one on whom he might confer the rule.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Hating all the great states,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He turned his kind regards on the west,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And there gave a settlement (to king {{tooltip|Thâi|Tài}}).

(King Thâi) raised up and removed{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The dead trunks and the fallen trees.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He dressed and regulated{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The bushy clumps and the (tangled) rows.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He opened up and cleared{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The tamarisk trees and the stave trees.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He hewed and thinned{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The mountain mulberry trees.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
God having brought about the removal thither of this intelligent ruler,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The {{tooltip|Kwan|Huàn}} hordes fled away<ref>The same as 'the hordes of the [[wikt:混|Khwăn]]' in [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/The Major Odes of the Kingdom/Decade 1/Ode 3|ode 3]]. Mr. [[Author:Thomas William Kingsmill|T.&#8239;W. Kingsmill]] says that '[[wikt:串|Kwan]]' here should be 'Chun,' and charges the transliteration Kwan with error ([[Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society]] for April, 1878). He had not consulted his dictionary for the proper pronunciation of the Chinese character.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Heaven had raised up a helpmeet for him,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And the appointment he had received was made sure.

God surveyed the hills,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Where the oaks and the buckthorn were thinned,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And paths made through the firs and cypresses.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
God, who had raised the<noinclude><!--¶-->
